issues.explanation: constraint "Alerts must support explanations understandable to a plant manager; explanation usefulness needs explicit user evaluation." has no source cited in facts; add a fact with the source recordId "C001-CH1", field "detail", quote "We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language."

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go: the selected configuration’s upper 95% confidence bound is below 5% separately on the bank-client population, initially and after vocabulary updates; updates require no full re-index; agreed maintenance and latency caps hold; and a prototype is testable within six months and approximately EUR 8,000 tooling/data expenditure.

sources.quote: our users freely switch between Latin and Cyrillic script mid-sentence — sometimes mid-word in typos.

We need an approach that handles lemmatisation or indexing in a way that is accurate for Serbian, tolerates script mixing automatically, and can be updated when new vocabulary arrives without a full re-index.
today we serve four banks and two telecoms providers across Serbia

issues.explanation: The bank-only aggregate gate can pass despite unacceptable telecom performance or persistent failures on within-word mixing and unseen terminology; merely evaluating those cases does not constrain acceptance. Add separate, pre-agreed acceptance rules for telecom and the required mixing/new-vocabulary strata, retaining constructed probes as a separate evaluation rather than automatically imposing the bank’s below-5% target on every stratum.

issues.claim: If reproduction passes, use the supported mechanism and a calibrated structural model to select welding, filler or geometry changes on tuning specimens.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be understanding exactly what is causing the cracks so we can change our welding procedure, filler material, or joint design and stop the warranty replacements.

issues.explanation: The reproduction gate can pass even if every condition, including the room-temperature reference, produces indistinguishable cracking, so it does not establish which factors or interactions explain the field failure. Require prespecified held-out factorial contrasts with an uncertainty-aware decision rule before calling a mechanism supported, and classify reproduction without discriminating contrasts as inconclusive.

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go: reproduce the observed connection location and fracture features in at least two of three evaluation replicates of the best-supported condition, with measured exposures reproduced and uncertainty reported.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

issues.explanation: The two-of-three rule leaves the counted fracture-match event and treatment of ambiguous field-to-laboratory matches undefined, and reproducing an exposure spectrum does not specify how long a specimen may be cycled before a crack counts as successful reproduction. Make evaluation conditional on freezing a field-informed matching rubric, uncertain-match handling and an exposure/censoring window before held-out testing; otherwise generic eventual fatigue cracking could satisfy the gate.

issues.claim: Proposed go/no-go: at least 80% of fully annotated injected episodes detected within 60 seconds of onset; the alert-burden criterion below; at least 80% correct identification of changed behaviour and appropriate next action by representative plant managers
issues.explanation: Neither 80% target states a statistical acceptance condition, and the explanation target does not define the scored unit, denominator, repeated-user handling or treatment of incomplete answers; small or repeatedly scored samples could therefore pass without sufficient evidence. Add a compact prerequisite defining episode matching and explanation scoring, repeat handling, and a confidence-bound or equivalent acceptance rule for each target, retaining separate protocol evaluation.

issues.claim: Propose counting all alert episodes, merging flagged non-overlapping ten-second windows within each site/protocol when gaps are at most 60 seconds. Divide by observed site/protocol-days; require an upper 95% day-block-bootstrap bound of one episode/day separately per protocol, retaining unresolved alerts.

sources.quote: it flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.

issues.explanation: Transitive merging permits an always-flagging detector to produce one long episode, pass the episode-rate bound and detect injected scenarios while failing the company's usable-alert objective. Retain episode counting but add an agreed acceptance limit on flagged-time exposure or persistent-alert duration, or cap merging duration so persistent false alerting cannot disappear from the burden measure.
